evals.name: debug-calling-convention-error
evals.prompt: I have a Clojure function that's failing with a NullPointerException. The function is (defn process [& [{:keys [id name email]}]] (str id ":" name ":" email)). When I call it like (process :id 1 :name "Alice" :email "alice@example.com") it fails. Help me debug this using REPL inspection to understand what's being passed to the function, and then test a fix before I modify the source code.
evals.expected_output: Guide user through capturing the map argument with inline def, inspecting it, discovering the calling convention is wrong, testing the fix in nrepl, then updating source code

evals.name: debug-missing-field-transform
evals.prompt: My test is calling (transform-user user-data) and getting a KeyError on :permissions. The function should map users to have a :permissions field, but it's missing in the output. I can run code in my REPL. Walk me through how to capture intermediate values at the point where the field should be added, inspect what's happening, form a hypothesis about the bug, and verify a fix works before I change the source.
evals.expected_output: Guide user through inline def to capture intermediate value, inspect structure, form hypothesis, test fix in nrepl, then commit with confidence

evals.name: debug-data-transformation-bug
evals.prompt: I'm debugging a function (defn process-records [records] (map #(update % :timestamp (fn [ts] (parse-date ts))) records)). Some records are returning nil for timestamp after processing. Help me use REPL-based inspection to understand what data is flowing through the transformation, identify where it's going wrong, test a fix, and confirm it works before modifying the actual source file.
evals.expected_output: Guide through capturing individual record, inspecting timestamp before/after transform, forming hypothesis, testing corrected transformation in nrepl, then updating source
